title: 7-Day Sri Lanka Itinerary: Culture & Nature — Colombo to Galle via the Hill Country
description: Ancient rock fortresses, sacred temples, the world's most scenic train ride, misty tea plantations, and golden southern beaches — Sri Lanka packs an almost unfair amount into one small island. This 7-day route covers the classic cultural triangle and hill country loop, ending with a coastal finale in Galle.

activities.name: Arrive at Bandaranaike International Airport
activities.description: Land at CMB airport (in Katunayake, 30km north of Colombo). Pick up your SIM card at the airport counter — Dialog has the best coverage. Colombo's seaside promenade — Galle Face Green is where locals fly kites and eat isso wade (shrimp fritters) at sunset. Walk to the nearby Dutch Hospital for craft shops and restaurants in a restored colonial building.
details: 💡 Airport to Colombo: ~1.5 hours by car (expressway). Use a taxi or your driver.
🦀 Ministry of Crab is here — Sri Lanka's most famous restaurant. Book ahead for their legendary mud crab.
📸 Galle Face Green is the classic Colombo sunset spot — arrive by 5pm.
tips: Don't spend too long in Colombo — one evening is enough. The magic is upcountry.

activities.name: Pettah Market (if time allows)
activities.description: If you arrived early enough, duck into Pettah — Colombo's most chaotic and vibrant market district. Spices, textiles, electronics, produce — sensory overload.
details: ⏰ Pettah closes by 7pm. Best before 5pm when it's buzzing.

activities.name: Drive to Dambulla (4–5 hours from Colombo)
activities.description: Early start north through rice paddies, rubber plantations, and small villages. Stop for a king coconut at any roadside stand. A UNESCO World Heritage Site with five caves filled with 150+ Buddha statues and ceiling paintings dating back to the 1st century BC. Built into a massive rock overhang with panoramic views.
details: 🚗 Leave by 6am to beat Colombo traffic. The A6 highway is the fastest route.
💰 Entry: $10 for foreigners. Go early to avoid heat and crowds.
📸 Cave 2 (Temple of the Great Kings) is the most impressive — 40+ seated Buddhas in a row.

activities.name: Continue to Sigiriya (30 min from Dambulla)
activities.description: Check into your hotel near Sigiriya. The area is rural and peaceful — monkeys, paddy fields, and stunning sunsets. Hike Pidurangala Rock for sunset — the neighboring rock with the BEST view of Sigiriya. Much cheaper ($5 vs $30), less crowded, and more photogenic. The final scramble over boulders is the fun part.
details: 🏨 Stay near Sigiriya village for easy access to both Sigiriya Rock and Pidurangala.
⏱️ 30-45 min hike up. Bring water and a flashlight for the descent.
📸 The sunset view of Sigiriya from Pidurangala is the most iconic photo in Sri Lanka.

days.title: Lion Rock & the Road to Kandy

activities.name: Climb Sigiriya Rock Fortress
activities.description: The 5th-century 'Lion Rock' — a 200m-tall rock plateau with the ruins of King Kashyapa's sky palace on top. Climb takes about 1.5 hours. Highlights: Mirror Wall, Sigiriya Frescoes, and the giant lion paw entrance.
details: 💰 Entry: $30 for foreigners (pricey but worth it).
⏰ Gates open at 7am — be there at opening to beat tour groups. Brutally hot after 10am.
🐝 Wasp nests on the rock face occasionally cause path closures. Ask at the gate.
tips: Wear sturdy shoes (not flip-flops), bring 1.5L water minimum, and don't bring food — monkeys will snatch it.

activities.name: Drive to Kandy (3 hours from Sigiriya)
activities.description: The drive south through the dry zone into the central highlands is gorgeous — the landscape shifts from flat scrubland to misty green hills. Optional stop at Matale spice gardens. Walk around the picturesque lake in the center of Kandy. The city sits in a valley surrounded by green hills — Sri Lanka's cultural capital with a different energy from the coast.
details: 🌿 Spice gardens: interesting to see cinnamon, pepper, cardamom growing. Skip the hard sell.

activities.name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
activities.description: Kandy's most sacred site — this ornate temple complex houses what's believed to be a tooth of the Buddha. The evening puja (6:30pm) is the most atmospheric time, with drumming, chanting, and the inner chamber briefly opened. Traditional Kandyan dance show — fire-walking, acrobatic drumming, and elaborate costumes. Shows around 5pm, last an hour. Touristy but genuinely impressive.
details: 💰 Entry: $10. Dress modestly — shoulders and knees covered, shoes off.
🙏 The tooth itself is inside golden caskets — you won't see it directly, but the ceremony is stunning.
💰 ~$10. Book at your hotel or just show up.

days.title: The World's Most Scenic Train Ride

activities.name: Kandy to Ella Train (6–7 hours)
activities.description: This is it — the reason half of travelers come to Sri Lanka. The train winds through emerald tea plantations, misty mountains, over bridges, and through tunnels. Consistently rated one of the most beautiful train journeys on Earth. The blue trains chug along at a pace that lets you hang out the open doorways.
details: 🚂 Trains depart Kandy at 8:47am and 11:10am. The 8:47am is less crowded.
💺 Book 2nd class reserved — 1st class has sealed windows (no photos!). 2nd unreserved works if you arrive early.
📸 Sit RIGHT going to Nuwara Eliya, then LEFT from Nuwara Eliya to Ella for best views.
🎫 Book at seat61.com/SriLanka or Kandy station one day before. ~$3 for 2nd class.
tips: The train often runs 30-60 minutes late. Don't schedule anything tight after arrival.

activities.name: Arrive in Ella & Settle In
activities.description: Ella is a tiny hill station at 1,000m elevation with a backpacker vibe — guesthouses, cafes, and stunning viewpoints everywhere. Noticeably cooler than the lowlands. Check in and take a short evening walk.
details: 🏨 Stay on the edge of town for quieter spots with views. Ella is small enough to walk everywhere.

activities.name: Sunrise at Little Adam's Peak
activities.description: A 45-minute hike through tea plantations to a panoramic viewpoint. Easy walk — not a serious climb. 360° views of Ella Gap are spectacular at sunrise.
details: ⏰ Leave by 5:30am for sunrise. Trail starts near 98 Acres Resort.
🥾 Easy hike, all fitness levels. Wear closed shoes for the damp trail.

activities.name: Nine Arches Bridge
activities.description: Sri Lanka's most Instagrammed spot — a colonial-era stone viaduct arching through dense jungle. Trains cross roughly every 2 hours. The walk from Ella town takes about 30 minutes through tea fields.
details: 🚂 Trains cross approximately at 9:05am, 11:00am, and 2:30pm — schedules are approximate.
📸 Best photos from the hill on the south side. Arrive 20 min before the train.
⚠️ Stand well clear of the tracks when a train approaches.

activities.name: Tea Factory Visit
activities.description: Visit a working tea factory to see how Ceylon tea goes from leaf to cup. The Uva region around Ella produces some of Sri Lanka's finest teas. A 25-meter waterfall right on the main road, 6km from Ella. Named after the demon king Ravana from the Ramayana.
details: 🍵 Dambatenne Tea Factory (built by Sir Thomas Lipton in 1890) is 40 min from Ella. Hike to Lipton's Seat viewpoint nearby.
💰 Factory tours: $2-5. Taste and buy fresh tea.
📸 Quick photo stop — 15 minutes is enough unless you want to wade in the pool.
tips: Ella is at elevation — evenings are cool (15-18°C in April). Bring a light layer.

activities.name: Drive from Ella to Galle (5–6 hours)
activities.description: The longest drive of the trip — from the cool highlands down through Yala-adjacent scrubland and along the dramatic southern coast. The landscape shifts from mountains to tropical lowlands to palm-fringed beaches.
details: 🚗 Leave early (7am) to have the full afternoon in Galle.
🐘 Optional: add a morning game drive at Yala National Park (5:30am from Ella) — but it adds a full extra day.
tips: Want a beach day? Break this drive with an overnight in Mirissa or Unawatuna.

activities.name: Explore Galle Fort
activities.description: The jewel of Sri Lanka's south coast — a 17th-century Dutch colonial fort, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the island's most atmospheric town. Cobblestone streets, boutique shops, art galleries, cafes, and ramparts overlooking the Indian Ocean. Join locals and travelers on the ramparts for sunset — a daily ritual in Galle. The lighthouse glows gold and cricket games break out below.
details: 🏰 Walk the full fort walls at sunset — 30-minute circuit with phenomenal views.
🕌 Key sites: Dutch Reformed Church, Galle Lighthouse, National Maritime Museum.
🛍️ Great shopping — local designers, hand-printed textiles, and Sri Lankan tea brands.
📸 Best spots: Flag Rock and the rampart near the lighthouse.

activities.name: Unawatuna Beach (or Jungle Beach)
activities.description: A 10-minute tuk-tuk from Galle Fort to one of Sri Lanka's best swimming beaches. Unawatuna is a sheltered crescent of golden sand with warm, calm water. For something more secluded, walk 10 minutes further to Jungle Beach — a tiny cove backed by forest. One of Sri Lanka's best breakfast spots — crisp egg hoppers with three house-made sambals (mild to properly spicy), served in a casual open-air spot near the sea.
details: 🏖️ Unawatuna is great for a morning swim. Jungle Beach is quieter and more photogenic.
🐢 If you're lucky, you might spot sea turtles near the reef.
🍳 Egg hoppers are the quintessential Sri Lankan breakfast — a bowl-shaped rice flour crepe with a runny egg in the center.
tips: Galle to the airport is 2.5-3 hours on the Southern Expressway. Budget extra time for potential traffic.

activities.name: Last Galle Fort Stroll & Souvenir Shopping
activities.description: Final walk through the fort streets. Pick up Ceylon tea, handmade soap, batik prints, or local spices as souvenirs. The Stick No Bills poster shop and Barefoot boutique are local favorites. Take the Southern Expressway from Galle to Colombo, then the airport expressway. Smooth, modern highway the whole way.
details: 🛍️ Stick No Bills: vintage-style Sri Lanka travel posters — great gifts.
🍵 Buy tea from any fort shop or directly from plantations — it's a fraction of export prices.
Leave 4+ hours before your flight to be safe.
